newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovakia,Czech Rep say to keep import restrictions.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia,Czech Rep say to keep import restrictions.

text.p: Slovakia and the Czech Republic said on Friday they would not immediately abolish import deposits despite complaints from the EU and the Central Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) countries.
Both countries introduced a 20 percent six-month deposit on most imports in April in order to solve their balance of payments problems.

"Our (Slovakia) measures will most probably only last until the end of the year when deposits will be abolished or reduced," Jan Foltin, Slovakia's State Secretary for Economy, told a news conference following the CEFTA meeting in Slovenia's tourist resort of Bled.
"The deposits are only temporary and our goal is to abolish them as soon as possible," Karel Kuhnl, Czech Minister of Industry and Trade, said.
Foltin also said Slovakia was considering alternative measures that would replace deposits in line with the European Union requests.
"We are considering a replacement of deposits possibly by special import charges because deposits hurt small and medium-sized companies much more than large ones," he said.
Foltin said the matter would be discussed at Slovakia's meeting with the European Union subcommittee on July 9.

"All CEFTA countries are in transition therefore there are significant ups and falls in their economies which makes it hard for them to insist on free trade principles," said Slovenia's Minister of Economic Relations and Development Marjan Senjur, who headed the meeting.
"As a consequence they sometimes have to implement trade restrictions but our goal is to make those as few as possible and to ensure they are only temporary," Senjur added.
Poland, which raised some import duties for CEFTA members from January, also said it would not abolish them immediately but would do so as soon as conditions permitted.
CEFTA, established in December 1992, currently comprises Slovenia, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, Hungary and Romania.
